---
title: "Resume a scan"
description: "Let customers continue capture after refreshing the page or returning later."
---

Save the scan ID on your customer’s application record when your backend creates it. Use that same scan when the customer returns to the capture page.

## Restore capture

<Steps>
  <Step title="Recover the customer's scan">
    Load the scan ID from the authenticated customer’s application or server-side session. The [backend example](/external/backend) reuses this ID when loading onboarding data.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Issue a fresh initialization token">
    Call `POST /v1/scans/:scan_id/capture-authorizations` for the existing scan with your registered capture-page origin. Return its `access_token` as `token`, together with `encodeConfiguration(apiUrl, scanId)`, through your onboarding response or page props.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Mount the capture screen">
    Pass the new `token` and `configuration` to the [React component](/external/web). Its initialization effect calls `instance.start()` and restores the scan identified by the configuration.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Once `state.resumable` is true, Bouncr has accepted the first capture and can restore that progress. The SDK requests the remaining side. If capture is already complete, it proceeds to processing status. A refresh before the first accepted capture requires the customer to capture again.

<Note>
  Store the scan reference on your backend. Request a fresh initialization token when reopening the page; keep the token out of persistent browser storage.
</Note>

## Handle another active window

When another window or device takes over the scan, the previous instance enters `Phase.SUPERSEDED`. Show a message directing the customer to continue in the other window. Offer a deliberate **Continue here** action if your product allows switching back.

## Finish the flow

After processing finishes, continue to your application's next screen:

```javascript
onComplete(scanId) {
  window.location.assign('/onboarding/review');
}
```

Keep the scan ID on your backend record so you can [retrieve its result](/external/results) later.
